text:
Oliver Bonk is the rookie Flyers fans have started arguing about in a good way. The 22nd pick in 2023, out of the London Knights, has seven points in 16 games on 18 minutes a night, and NHL.com's Rookie Watch had him "earning trust" in Philadelphia. Broad Street Hockey went further, suggesting the Flyers may have underestimated his offensive ceiling.

His results are, if anything, unlucky. The Flyers have scored 6.7 fewer goals than their chances with him on, and they're more than five points better in shot share with him than without. That's a lot to ask of a 21-year-old on a team that loses the chance battle most nights. Seven points in 16 games is well ahead of the 0.21 points a game that is the median for defensemen picked 17th to 27th in their first full seasons.

There's a wrinkle: his minutes have dropped lately, under 15 in each of the last two games, nearly three a night below his average. On a team where the coaching staff's choices are under a microscope, that's worth watching. The puck-moving profile (he plays like Thomas Chabot, by our comparison) is the reason to keep him on the ice.
